What is here. Every agenda item at a full Metro Council meeting where Metro's official record lists how each member voted. We scanned 12,156 agenda items from 75 full council meetings in Legistar dated 2023-10-03 to 2026-11-05. 480 items have an individual vote record, adding up to 19,142 individual votes from 70 meetings (2023-10-03 to 2026-11-05). Items decided by voice vote, on consent without a recorded tally, deferred, withdrawn, or referred without a vote have no individual record and are not listed. Nothing on this page is estimated or filled in.

Important coverage note. Through August 2026, Legistar lists individual votes for only a few items per meeting, mostly contested ones: 213 items, 194 of which had at least one no vote. Starting September 2026, Legistar lists individual votes for nearly every item (267 items in 5 meetings), including routine ones that passed unanimously. So for 2023 to mid-2026 this page is a strong record of divided votes but not of every routine vote, and per-member vote counts lean toward recent months. Attendance uses roll calls, so it is not affected.

Attendance method. For each full council meeting we use the opening roll call recorded in Legistar (75 of 75 meetings have one). A member marked Present counts as attending. A member marked Absent at roll call who then cast a recorded vote that night counts as attending, since they arrived late. For meetings with no recorded roll call, a member counts as attending if they cast at least one recorded vote (yes, no, abstain, present, or recused) and as missing it if every recorded vote lists them absent. Test entries, a cancelled meeting, and State of Metro addresses are not counted. Meetings with neither a roll call nor any recorded votes are also left out of every member's total. Each member's total only counts meetings held while they were seated. "Absent for votes" is a separate count: a member can attend a meeting but be listed absent on some votes if they stepped out or did not vote.

Other definitions. "With the majority" is the share of a member's yes and no votes that matched the side with more votes on that item. "Present, not voting" is mostly the Vice Mayor, who presides and votes only to break a tie. Former members who voted earlier in the term appear in the full roll calls as "Former member."

Known gaps. Legistar has no full council meetings for September 2023, the first month of this term, so those meetings are not included. Consent agenda items are often adopted together in one vote, which the record may repeat under each item. Committee votes are not included, only full council meetings. Committee lists come from each member's nashville.gov page and may lag current assignments.

What this page cannot tell you. Why anyone voted the way they did. For that, open the meeting page linked from each item for the agenda, minutes and video, watch the Metro Nashville Network recordings, or read the member's newsletter.

Sources. Votes and attendance: Metro's public Legistar records (nashville.legistar.com, read through the public API at webapi.legistar.com/v1/nashville). District lines: the Metro GIS Council Districts layer. Photos, biographies, phone numbers and committee lists: each member's page on nashville.gov. Newsletter links were checked by hand. Archive links go to Nashville Newsletters. To cross-check, see the Nashville Pamphleteer council tracker and Metro Minutes.
